description: Project Resource Allocation / Deallocation Ticketing (New Allocation, Request Replacement, Update Allocation, Deallocation, Direct Allocate)
edgeCases: Multi-resource New Allocation submission (e.g., 5–10 resources in one form) must generate one separate ticket per resource, each independently trackable.

Shadow-developer count increases an employee's total available allocation % by 100% per shadow assignment (e.g., 1 shadow dev → up to 200% available, 2 → 300%), which can produce unusually high displayed availability values (e.g. 140%).
Selecting a candidate whose available % is below the requested allocation % must render the row/box with a red warning highlight and block further action.
Reducing allocation by ≥70% relative to current allocation triggers mandatory rating/feedback capture before the decrease ticket can be submitted; reductions <70% do not require this.
Resulting allocation <10% surfaces a system suggestion to fully deallocate instead of partially reducing.

Ticket list KPI tiles (All / Open / In Review / Awaiting / Approved) must sum consistently — an observed case in the walkthrough showed 'All Tickets' = 46 while a filtered tile alone displayed 61, an inconsistent state.
Applied filters on the project allocation/ticket list must persist when the user navigates away to another tab and returns, without being reset.
A user holding both TM and PM roles must see two independently-scoped ticket tabs (Project Tickets as PM, Department Tickets as TM) with no data bleed between them.
Duplicating an existing ticket (to add resource #2, #3, etc.) must copy all prior field values except tech-stack selections, which must remain independently editable per duplicated ticket.

PMO's direct allocate/deallocate action from the Employee Details page must generate a placeholder ticket in the ticket list purely for audit/reporting, without invoking the shortlisting/approval workflow.

Create or update an allocation ticket via the UI, then fetch the same ticket via its API endpoint and confirm the returned allocation %, status, and department match exactly (regression-derived, API/UI parity risk).

Double-click or rapidly re-submit the New Allocation (or Replacement/Update) ticket submit button and verify only one ticket is created, not duplicates (regression-derived, double-submit risk on a Create flow).

After a Deallocation ticket is applied, verify the employee no longer appears in the project's active team-member list or in shortlisting dropdowns for that project (regression-derived, stale-reference risk after a status transition).

Attempt to force a ticket directly from 'Open' to 'Approved & Applied' (skipping shortlisting/approval) via the UI and via a direct API call; both must be rejected (regression-derived, invalid state-machine transition risk).

After PMO performs a direct allocate/deallocate action from Employee Details, verify the placeholder ticket appears in the ticket list immediately without a manual page refresh (regression-derived, cache-refresh risk).
Apply a ticket-list filter combination that matches zero tickets and verify an explicit empty-state message is shown rather than a blank or stale list (regression-derived, filtering edge case).
businessRules: Each role's permitted and forbidden actions (PM/TM/PMO department-selection, approval rights, bypass rights) must be enforced at both UI level (control hidden/disabled) and API level (403 on unauthorized action)
Submitting the same allocation/replacement/update ticket form twice in quick succession (double-click or rapid resubmit) must not create duplicate tickets
Any allocation/ticket data written via the UI (new ticket, status change, approval) must be retrievable via the corresponding API with identical values
A deallocated employee must not appear as an active team member in the project's team list, active dropdowns, or shortlisting candidate pools

Allocation tickets must only progress through valid status transitions (Open → Department Assigned → Shortlisting → Awaiting Approval → Approved & Applied, or → Bypassed, or → Rejected back to Shortlisting); no status may be skipped or set arbitrarily
After PMO's direct allocate/deallocate action or any ticket status change, the ticket list and project team-member list must reflect the change immediately without requiring a manual page refresh
